chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Part of the perfection of Hajj and 'Umrah is that you enter into the state of Ihram from the Miqat (stations of entering Ihram) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated. Do not pass them unless you are in the state of Ihram. For he designated for the people of Iraq, and at that time there was no Iraq [as a specific region], the Belly of al-'Aqiq from the side of the people of Iraq. And he designated for the people of Yemen, Yalamlam. And he designated for the people of Ta'if, Qarn al-Manazil. And he designated for the people of the Maghreb (West), al-Juhfa, which is Mahya'ah. And he designated for the people of Medina, Dhu al-Hulayfah. And whoever's dwelling is behind these Miqat stations, from the side facing Mecca, then his Miqat is his dwelling."
ai.seo_question: What are the designated Miqat stations for Hajj and 'Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Miqat stations as a fundamental pillar of Hajj validity, emphasizing the Prophet’s precise geographical delineations for various regions. It clarifies the legal principle that residents living beyond these designated boundaries must assume the state of Ihram at their own homes, ensuring uniformity in ritual preparation. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the Sunnah’s specific spatial and temporal markers for pilgrimage rites.
